question: Why did the error rate go up on 21 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of catalog v3.27 to eu-west caused the error rate to rise.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v3.27 introduced a new version of the service.
The new version of the service interacted with the upstream catalog-db, causing it to return HTTP 503.
The catalog-db timeout retries caused the service to experience increased latency and error rates.

contributing_factors.description: The catalog-db is experiencing degraded performance, which is affecting the service catalog.
why_chain: The catalog-db is an upstream service used by the service catalog.
The catalog-db is experiencing degraded performance, indicated by the HTTP 503 status.
The degraded performance of the catalog-db is causing the service catalog to experience increased latency and error rates.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a sudden increase in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for service catalog did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change in the service catalog.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate change is concentrated in the service catalog, not in other service/region segments.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog rose from 0.42% to 5.47% (+1217%), with a change point at 2026-03-21T15:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.06).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog stayed about the same (1704 per 5 min before, 1901 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog rose (120 ms before, 216 ms after, +80%).
Upstream catalog-db returning HTTP 503 for catalog (catalog; 2 min after the change; record R017)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, eu-west; 7 min after the change; record R018)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, us-east; 17 min after the change; record R019)
Deployed catalog v3.27 to eu-west (catalog, eu-west; 224 min before the change; record R014)
catalog-db status page: investigating degraded performance (catalog; 30 min after the change; record R021)

reasons: ✓ A change event (alerts) lines up in time (2 min after the change).
✓ 3 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Roll back the catalog v3.27 deployment to eu-west.
Monitor the catalog-db for any further issues and ensure it is performing optimally.
Review and optimize the retry logic for the catalog-db calls in the service catalog.
